workLog.action: Read issue #3357 and confirmed the defect against the driver source
workLog.result: main() wrote the merge result with Path.write_text, which truncates the destination before writing. A partial write leaves a damaged graph in git %A, and the nonzero exit tells git to keep exactly that instead of falling back to ours.

workLog.action: Replaced the write with a sibling temporary and a rename
workLog.result: Failures before the rename leave the destination byte-identical and the temporary is unlinked on the way out. The destination mode is read first and reapplied, because mkstemp creates at 0600 and os.replace carries the temporary mode.

workLog.action: Updated the exit-3 test and added coverage for the acceptance criteria
workLog.result: The old test drove the failure through Path.write_text, which the driver no longer calls, so it failed. It now fails os.replace. Five tests cover byte-identity after a refused rename and after a refused mid-payload write, no temporary left behind, and a preserved mode on success. 68 pass, up from 63.
Restoring the plain write turns 3 red, dropping the chmod turns 1 red, dropping the temporary cleanup turns 2 red.

patterns.pattern: A test that fails when the implementation changes shape is evidence the change is real
patterns.context: The exit-3 test monkeypatched Path.write_text, the exact call the fix removes.
patterns.application: Read the failure as confirmation, then rewrite the test against the new failure point rather than preserving the old patch target.

avoidances.antipattern: Assuming os.replace preserves the destination mode
avoidances.consequence: mkstemp creates at 0600, so the merged graph would have come back private to whoever ran the merge.
avoidances.correction: Read the destination mode before the write and reapply it to the temporary before the rename.
